question: Should OpenClaw adopt this strict one-feature/one-global-two-part-ID QA taxonomy contract, including the intentional smoke-ci and release profile narrowing?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent but changes the semantic meaning of maintained QA coverage and selector outputs across the taxonomy; automated repair cannot determine whether the reduced claimed coverage is the desired long-term policy.

options.title: Accept the strict QA contract
options.body: Approve the one-ID-per-feature model after resolving the exact-head failures and confirming the profile reductions accurately reflect the fixed smoke plan.

options.title: Keep broader profile accounting
options.body: Ask for a narrower follow-up that preserves current smoke/release selectors while separately introducing unambiguous coverage ownership.

options.title: Pause for a QA design decision
options.body: Defer the migration until QA owners document the intended relationship between executable scenarios, taxonomy features, and profile eligibility.

recommendation.title: Accept the strict QA contract
recommendation.body: Approve the one-ID-per-feature model after resolving the exact-head failures and confirming the profile reductions accurately reflect the fixed smoke plan.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current QA migration and are the best available routing point for its reconciliation rationale; final acceptance remains a maintainer QA-policy decision.
